drivingQuestion: What does 'if he remarried her' add, given the mishna on remarrying on the first ketuba?

segments.he: הֶחְזִירָה — הֲרֵי הִיא כְּכׇל הַנָּשִׁים, וְאֵין לָהּ אֶלָּא כְּתוּבָּתָהּ. הֶחְזִירָה, מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? תְּנֵינָא: הַמְגָרֵשׁ אֶת הָאִשָּׁה וּמַחְזִירָה, עַל מְנָת כְּתוּבָּה רִאשׁוֹנָה מַחְזִירָהּ!
segments.en: It was further taught in the mishna that if he «remarried her, she is like all women, and she has nothing other» than «her marriage contract.» The Gemara asks: «What is» the tanna «teaching us» by mentioning the possibility that he «remarried her? We» already «learned» this: With regard to «one who divorces a woman and remarries her, he remarries her on the basis of» her «first marriage contract,» and he need not write her a new one. Why is it necessary to emphasize this halakha in the case of a yevama?
